senses.gloss:
Jahāṅgīra
Moghul Emperor; patron of Kṛṣṇa Daivajña (a. of C. on Bhāskara's Bījagaṇita etc. See NCC. IV. p. 323b); Rudrakavi (a. of Navābakhānacaritra, IO. 7304); Paramānanda Jyotiṣarāya (a. of Jahāṅgīravinodaratnākara, Bikaner 4605).
For a list of Skt. writers of the period of Jahangir see Sri Ram Sharma, A Bibl. of Mughal India p.. 157-60.
For a Skt. verse (Beg. zyAmaM yajJopavItaM tava kimiti maSI) in praise of Jahangir, see J. B. Chaudhuri, Muslim Patronage to Skt. Learning p. 100.

Jahāṅgīracarita
by Rudrakavi, son of Ananta; mentioned in the intro. to GOS. [Page207-b] edition V. (1917) of Rāṣtrauḍhavam3śa (Mahākāvya), another work of the author.

Jahāṅgīravinodaratnākara
jy. by Paramānanda Jyotiṣarāya, patronized by Jahangir; written under the direction of Itvarkhan. Bikaner 4605. Mithilā.

Jahnu
poet. Skm. p.. 4. 246 (Lahore edn.). verse nos. 7. 1788 (Calcutta edn.). See also Āvantikajahnu. NCC. II. p. 185b. (Skm. verse 793. 1145. 1255).

Jahnubhaṭṭa
16th Cent. of Kāṇvaśākhā, Śukla Yv. father of Nāgadeva (Nāgeśa) an. grandfather of Ananta Bhaṭṭa (a. of Vidhānapārijāta, IO. 1468).
See also JASB. Proceed. 1904. p. 19.

Jāhnavyaṣṭaka
in praise of Jāhnavī, daughter of Sūryadāsa an. cousin of Rādhā an. one of the beloved devotees of Lord Kṛṣṇa. (Beg. anaGgamaJjarIkhyAte vraje) by Jīvagosvāmin. MT. 3053 (x).

Jāhnavyaṣṭaka
by Dāmodara Gosvāmin.
Pt.. Stavamālā 1860. 1876. See IO. Pt.. Bk.. 1938, p. 1127.
